name: end of life decisions overview
title: End of life: a patient who cannot decide gets a substitute decision maker in a fixed order; palliative care is reached by four routes and aims at comfort; a patient who asks for medical assistance in dying must meet every eligibility criterion, and the stream (natural death foreseeable or not) sets the safeguards

root.title: End of life: who decides, and what can be offered?
lines: capacity = UNDERSTAND the information + APPRECIATE the foreseeable consequences · specific to each decision · can fluctuate
code status (which resuscitation, if any) needs informed consent from the patient or SDM · it is NOT the same as goals of care

groups.title: Patient asks for medical assistance in dying (MAiD)

pres.title: Eligible? ALL of these
lines: • eligible for publicly funded health care
• grievous and irremediable: serious illness, advanced irreversible decline, unbearable suffering

head: h
Substitute decision maker (SDM)
gives or refuses consent for the patient
do: Ask the SDM, in this ORDER
WISHES that guide the SDM, NOT advance consent

head: h
Palliative care
quality of life: physical, psychosocial, spiritual · patient AND family
when: • treatment futile or would cause suffering
check: • Palliative Performance Scale: disease burden, progress to end of life
• Edmonton Symptom Assessment System: symptoms to manage
do: • stroke, disability unacceptable to them: no tube feeds or IV fluids
• turning and symptom drugs do NOT hasten death

head: h
Stream 1
natural death reasonably FORESEEABLE
do: Consent AGAIN at the time of MAiD
unless a WAIVER of final consent was signed (at risk of losing capacity)

head: h
Stream 2
natural death NOT reasonably foreseeable
check: ONE has expertise in the condition and has discussed all treatment options
do: consent AGAIN at the time of MAiD
